note: Authoritative flash/clock parameters for the two X-Plus 4 MCUs. Every value is DERIVED (never copied from a QIDI binary); 'evidence' says how. A board whose status is 'unresolved' is never built into a release bundle (mcu/build-mcu.sh gate) and never written by eitri-mcuflash (installer/mcuflash boards.json carries the same status). Keep this file and installer/mcuflash/eitri_mcuflash/boards.json in step; mcu/tests/test_params.py fails when they drift.

mainboard.bootloader: Stock QIDI/Makerbase bootloader at 0x08000000, about 32 KiB. Not Katapult. Two entry paths: a UART protocol (hid-flash, 115200 8N1) and the SD-card path (qd_mcu.bin to qd_mcu.CUR). Never deploy Katapult here: that overwrites the bootloader.
mainboard.bootloader_baud: 115200 8N1 for the hid-flash UART path (the application runs at 500000); not applicable to the SD path
mainboard.method: Application-only write, bootloader preserved. Preferred: Klipper scripts/flash-sdcard.sh -b 500000 /dev/ttyS0 qidi-plus4 (needs a running Klipper application and a FAT32 card in the slot). Fallback: copy the image as qd_mcu.bin to the SD card and power-cycle. The pinned Kalico has no qidi-plus4 board definition, so Kalico trees use the card fallback or the pinned Klipper script tree.
evidence: Measured on the printer 2026-10-22 (read-only debug_read, klippy stopped): SCB->VTOR = 0x08008000, DBGMCU_IDCODE 0x16423 (genuine STM32F401), flash 256 KiB, RCC_PLLCFGR 0x07412A04 = HSE source, M=4 N=168 P=4, i.e. 84 MHz from an 8 MHz crystal. The words at 0x08000000 are the bootloader's vector table (stack 0x20010000, reset 0x08004b95), those at 0x08008000 the application's.

Live klippy.log of the printer: MCU=stm32f401xc CLOCK_FREQ=84000000 RESERVE_PINS_crystal=PH0,PH1 RESERVE_PINS_serial=PA10,PA9 SERIAL_BAUD=500000 (an external crystal is present; its frequency is not printed).

Offset: a community Plus 4 mainboard Klipper image (not QIDI-authored) has its reset handler code at the position that is consistent only with a link address of 0x08008000, and boots on this board family; its data dictionary equals the live constants.
Crystal: the same image's PLL setting is the one that derives 84 MHz from an 8 MHz oscillator (PLL M = 4).
A working community mainline configuration for this printer selects STM32F401, FLASH_START_8000, CLOCK_REF_8M, USART1, 500000.
Upstream Klipper board_defs.py maps qidi-plus4 to the qidi-x7 definition (spi2, PB12, qd_mcu.bin / qd_mcu.CUR), and src/stm32/Kconfig maps STM32_FLASH_START_8000 to 0x8008000.

toolhead.mcu_note: A GD32F103 clone (DBGMCU_IDCODE 0x21040414, flash-size register 128 KiB, measured 2026-10-22); the stock firmware and Klipper build it as stm32f103xe.
toolhead.clock_ref: 8 MHz external crystal (STM32_CLOCK_REF_8M): RCC_CFGR 0x001DE40A = HSE, PLL x9, measured 2026-10-22.
toolhead.bootloader: None. Measured 2026-10-22: SCB->VTOR = 0x08000000 and the vector table at 0x08000000 is the Klipper application's own (stack 0x20005000, reset 0x08003afd). The factory firmware is a bare application, so there is no serial route to reflash it.
toolhead.bootloader_baud: Not applicable until Katapult is installed; Eitri's own Katapult build for this board uses 500000 (the application's rate).
toolhead.method: Not over serial: the factory image has no bootloader. Install Katapult once over SWD (ST-Link, docs/RECOVERY.md); from then on Katapult flashtool over /dev/ttyS2 writes the application at 0x08002000. eitri-mcuflash writes this board only while Katapult answers a read-only handshake (resolved_by katapult). Until then the toolhead keeps its stock Klipper v0.12 firmware, which the current host drives (accelerometer through [qd_adxl345_stock]).
evidence: Measured on the printer 2026-10-22 (read-only debug_read, klippy stopped): SCB->VTOR = 0x08000000, boot and application vector tables identical (stack 0x20005000, reset 0x08003afd), DBGMCU_IDCODE 0x21040414, flash 128 KiB, RCC_CFGR 0x001DE40A (HSE x9 = 72 MHz from 8 MHz). A full flash dump is kept privately as a recovery image.
Live klippy.log of the printer: MCU=stm32f103xe CLOCK_FREQ=72000000 RESERVE_PINS_serial=PB7,PB6 SERIAL_BAUD=500000.

A community Plus 4 toolhead Klipper image is linked at 0x08002000 (reset handler position, and a vector table beginning with a RAM-top stack pointer 0x20005000), consistent with Katapult's 8 KiB layout. It says nothing about the factory layout.
That image's clock setting is PLL x9, which gives 72 MHz from an 8 MHz crystal.
A Q2 toolhead image suggests 0x08008000 for a stock layout, but it was never observed on a Plus 4.
open_questions: Before the first Katapult install over SWD: settle STM32F103GD_DISABLE_SWD for this GD32 clone (SWD must stay usable for recovery) and freeze configs/toolhead-stm32f103.config for the 0x08002000 layout.

conflicts: None open. The toolhead question (Katapult or stock bootloader, 0x08002000 or 0x08008000) was settled by measurement on 2026-10-22: no bootloader at all, application at 0x08000000.
